nodes.name: Proof of the occupation-measure/stochastic-matrix correspondence
nodes.statement: Assume that $A\in \operatorname{Stoc}(n)$. Let $\mathbf{z}=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)^\top$ be the stationary distribution corresponding to $A$. So $\mathbf{z}$ is a probability vector satisfying $A^\top\mathbf{z}=\mathbf{z}$. A straightforward computation shows that $\mathop{{\rm diag}}\nolimits(\mathbf{z})A\in\Omega(n)$. We define $\Phi_n(A)$ to be the set of all occupation measures of this form. Hence $\Phi_n(A)$ is a closed convex set. This proves part \emph{1}. Furthermore $\Phi_n(A)$ consists of one occupation measure $\mu(A)$ if and only if $\mathbf{z}$ is unique, i.e., $1$ is a geometrically simple eigenvalue. It is a classical property of stochastic matrices that the geometric and algebraic multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$ coincide, see Theorem 6.5.3 in \cite{Fribook}; hence, $1$, is an algebraically simple eigenvalue. This proves part \emph{2}. Clearly, if $A$ is irreducible then $\mathbf{z}>\mathbf{0}$ is unique and $\mu(A)$ is irreducible. We now define $\Psi_n(\mu)$. Suppose first that $\mu$ does not have a zero row. Let $r_i=\sum_{j=1}^n \mu_{ij}$. Then $\Psi_n(\mu):=\mathop{{\rm diag}}\nolimits(r_1^{-1},\ldots,r_n^{-1})\mu$. Note that $\mathbf{z}=(r_1,\ldots,r_n)^\top$ is a probability vector satisfying $\Psi_n(\mu)^\top \mathbf{z}=\mathbf{z}$. Hence $\Phi_n(\Psi_n(\mu))$ contains $\mu$. Clearly, if $\mu$ is irreducible then $\Psi_n(\mu)$ is irreducible. Parts \emph{3} and \emph{4} follow straightforwardly. Assume now that $\mu$ has zero rows. Let $S(\mu)\subset [n]$ be the subset of all zero rows of $\mu$. As $\mu$ is an occupation measure, $S(\mu)$ is also the subset of zero columns of $\mu$. Let $k$ be the cardinality of $S(\mu)$. Then $\mu$ is a direct sum of $\mu_1\oplus 0_{k\times k}$, where $\mu_1\in\Omega(n-k)$ with nonzero rows, and $0_{k\times k}$ is the $k\times k$ zero matrix. Let $J_k\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}$ be the matrix whose all entries are $1$. Then $\Psi_n(\mu)=\Psi_{n-k}(\mu_1)\oplus \frac{1}{k}J_k$. Clearly, $\Phi_n(\Psi_n(\mu))$ contains $\mu$ in this case. This completes the proof of part \emph{5}.
nodes.statement_short: Define Phi_n(A) via stationary distributions diag(z)A and Psi_n by row normalization, padding zero rows uniformly.

nodes.statement_short: The correction terms cancel, giving log rho(A).

nodes.name: Proof of the entropic characterization for matrices
nodes.statement: Assume first that $A>0$. The for each $\mu>0$ we have inequality \eqref{auxlemAG1}. Hence \begin{eqnarray*} \log\rho(A)\geqslant\sup_{\mu=[\mu_{i,j}]\in\Omega(n), \mu>0} \sum_{i,j\in[n]} \mu_{ij}\log \frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n \mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}=\\ \sup_{\mu=[\mu_{i,j}]\in\Omega(n)} \sum_{i,j\in[n]} \mu_{ij}\log \frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n \mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}. \end{eqnarray*} Choose $\mu$ as in \eqref{maxmu} to deduce \eqref{AGchar1}. Assume now that $A\geqslant 0$ but not positive. First observe that if $a_{ij}=0$ and $\mu_{ij}>0$ then $\mu_{ij}\log\frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n\mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}=-\infty$. Hence $\sum_{i,j=1}^n \mu_{ij}\log\frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n\mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}=-\infty$. Suppose that $\rho(A)=0$. Then $\log\rho(A)=-\infty$. Since a support of $A$ does not contain a dicycle we deduce that $\sum_{i,j=1}^n \mu_{ij}\log\frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n\mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}=-\infty$ for each $\mu\in\Omega(n)$. Therefore \eqref{AGchar1} holds in this case. Suppose that $A=[a_{ij}]$ is irreducible. So $\log\rho(A)>-\infty$. The above arguments imply that it is enough to show \begin{equation} \log\rho(A)=\max_{\mu=[\mu_{i,j}]\in\Omega(n,\supp{A})} \sum_{i,j\in[n]} \mu_{ij}\log \frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n \mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}. \end{equation} For $\mu\in\Omega(n,\supp{A})$ such that $\supp{A}=\supp{\mu}$ we can use Lemma \ref{auxlemAG} to deduce \eqref{AGchar2} as for $A>0$. It is left to show for \eqref{AGchar1} for a nonnilpotent nonirreducible $A$. Let $J_n\in\mathbb{R}^{ns n}_+$, where each entry of $J_n$ is $1$. Consider $A(\varepsilon)=A+\varepsilon J_n$, where $\varepsilon>0$. Then $\rho(A)<\rho(A(\varepsilon)$. As $\log a_{ij}<\log(a_{ij}+\varepsilon)$, and the theorem holds for $A(\varepsilon)$, it follows that \[\log\rho(A(\varepsilon)) >\sup_{\mu=[\mu_{i,j}]\in\Omega(n)} \sum_{i,j\in[n]} \mu_{ij}\log \frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n \mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}.\] Letting $\varepsilon\searrow 0$ we deduce the inequality \[\log\rho(A)\geqslant\sup_{\mu=[\mu_{i,j}]\in\Omega(n)} \sum_{i,j\in[n]} \mu_{ij}\log \frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n \mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}.\] Assume that $A_1$ is an irreducible principle submatrix of $A$ such that $\rho(A)=\rho(A_1)$. Then $\supp (A_1)\subset S\times S$ for some minimal nonempty subset of $[n]$. Consider $\Omega(n,S\times S)$. Now apply the theorem for the irreducible $A_1$ to deduce the theorem in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Positive case from Lemma 18; then nilpotent, irreducible and reducible cases via supports and perturbation A + eps J.

nodes.name: Nilpotent case
nodes.statement: Assume now that $A\geqslant 0$ but not positive. First observe that if $a_{ij}=0$ and $\mu_{ij}>0$ then $\mu_{ij}\log\frac{a_{ij}\sum_{k=1}^n\mu_{ik}}{\mu_{ij}}=-\infty$. Therefore \eqref{AGchar1} holds in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Measures off the support give -infinity; nilpotent A has no dicycles.

nodes.name: Action simplex Pi_{i,n}
nodes.statement: The action space in state $i\in [n]$ is the simplex $\Pi_{i,n}:= \{p=(p_1,\dots,p_n)^T\in \Pi_n\mid a_{ij}=0 \implies p_j =0\}$, consisting of probability measures whose support is included in the support of the $i$th line of $A$.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius

nodes.name: Kullback-Leibler payment KL_i
nodes.statement: In state $i$, if the player selects action $p$, the next state becomes $j$ with probability $p_j$, and the player receives a payment, given by the Kullback-Leibler entropy \[ \operatorname{KL}_i(p,a):= - \sum_{j\in [n]} p_j \log (p_j/a_{ij}) \enspace , \] and the game is pursued in the same way, from the current state $j$.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius

nodes.name: Ergodic control problem
nodes.statement: The ergodic control problem consists in finding a strategy of the player which maximizes the expected average payment per time unit.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius

nodes.name: Value of a communicating ergodic game is state independent
nodes.statement: It is known that if such a game is communicating, meaning that for every states $i,j$, there is a strategy which ensures that the probability of reaching $j$ in finite time starting from state $i$ is positive, the value of the game is independent of the initial state.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius
conclusions: the value of the game is independent of the initial state

nodes.name: Communication equals irreducibility
nodes.statement: Here, the communication assumption is equivalent to the irreducibility of the matrix $A$.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius
conclusions: the communication assumption is equivalent to the irreducibility of the matrix $A$

nodes.name: Feedback policy
nodes.statement: Recall that a (feedback) {\em policy} is a map $\pi$ which associates to a state an admissible action in this state. So here, $\pi$ associates to $i$ a vector $\pi(i)\in \Pi_{i,n}$, and we may identify $\pi$ to the stochastic matrix with rows $\pi(i)$, $i\in [n]$.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius

nodes.name: Invariant measures M(pi)
nodes.statement: We denote by $M(\pi)$ the set of invariant measures of this matrix.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius

nodes.name: Value of ergodic game as maximum over policies and invariant measures
nodes.statement: It is known, still under the communication assumption, that the value of the game, for any initial state, coincides with the maximum over all policies $\pi$ and over all invariant measures $\theta\in M(\pi)$ of the expectation of the payment with respect to this measure, see \cite[Proposition 7.2]{AG03}.
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius
conclusions: the value of the game, for any initial state, coincides with the maximum over all policies $\pi$ and over all invariant measures $\theta\in M(\pi)$ of the expectation of the payment with respect to this measure

nodes.name: Ergodic control interpretation of the matrix entropic formula
nodes.statement_short: Specializing the ergodic-control value formula recovers the entropic characterization of log rho(A).
nodes.section: 6.2 Ergodic control interpretation of the spectral radius

nodes.name: Support of a tensor
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{T}=[t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$ we denote by $\supp \mathcal{T}$ the \emph{support} of the tensor $\mathcal{T}$, i.e., \[ \supp \mathcal{T}:= \{(i_1,\dots,i_d)\mid t_{i_1,\dots, i_d}>0 \} \enspace . \]
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Occupation measure (tensor)
nodes.statement: A tensor $\mu=[\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$ is called an {\em occupation measure} if \begin{eqnarray} &&\sum_{i_1\in [n],\dots, i_d\in [n]}\mu_{i_1,i_2,\dots, i_d}=1,\notag\\ &&\sum_{i_2,\dots,i_d\in [n]} \mu_{j,i_2,\dots,i_d} =(d-1) \displaystyle\sum_{(i_1,i_3,\dots,i_d)\in [n] } \mu_{i_1,j,i_3,\dots,i_d} \qquad \forall j\in [n]\enspace . \end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Equivalent flow condition for tensor occupation measures
nodes.statement: Note that in view of the partial symmetry of $\mu$ the condition \eqref{tenocmeas} is equivalent to \[\sum_{(i_2,\dots,i_d)\in[n]} \mu_{j,i_2,\dots,i_d} = \displaystyle\sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d\in [n],j\in (i_2,\dots,i_d) } \mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d} \qquad \forall j\in [n]\enspace . \]

assumptions: in view of the partial symmetry of $\mu$

nodes.name: Set of tensor occupation measures
nodes.statement: We denote by $\Omega(n^{\times (d-1)})\subset \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$ the set of occupation measures.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Tensor occupation measures supported in supp T
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$ we denote by $\Omega(n^{\times (d-1)},\supp \mathcal{T})\subseteq \Omega(n^{\times (d-1)})$ the set of occupation measures whose support is contained in $\supp \mathcal{T}$.

nodes.name: Entropic characterization of the spectral radius
nodes.statement: The spectral radius of $\mathcal{T}=[t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in \mathbb{R}_{ps.+}^{n^{\times d}}$ has the following characterization \begin{eqnarray} \log \rho(\mathcal{T}) &= \displaystyle \max_{\mu\in \Omega(n^{\times(d-1)})} \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d\in [n]} \mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d} \log \Big(\frac{(\sum_{k_2,\dots, k_d}\mu_{i_1,k_2,\dots, k_d})t_{i_1,\dots, i_d}}{\mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d}}\Big) \enspace . \end{eqnarray} Assume that $\mathcal{T}$ is weakly irreducible. Let $\mathbf{u}>0$ be the unique positive eigenvector $\mathbf{u}$ satisfying \eqref{poseigvec} and let $\mathbf{w}>\mathbf{0}$ be defined as in \eqref{defpropA}. Let $\mu=[\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$ be the tensor given by \begin{equation} \mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}=\frac{1}{\rho(\mathcal{T})} w_{i_1}u_{i_1}^{-(d-2)}t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}u_{i_2}\cdots u_{i_d} \textrm{ for } i_1,\ldots,i_d\in[n]. \end{equation} Then $\mu$ is an occupation measure whose support is $\supp \mathcal{T}$. Furthermore, \begin{equation} \log\rho(\mathcal{T})=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_d\in [n]} \mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d} \log \Big(\frac{(\sum_{k_2,\dots, k_d}\mu_{i_1,k_2\dots ,k_d})t_{i_1,\dots, i_d}}{\mu_{i_1,\dots ,i_d}}\Big) \enspace . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: log rho(T) is the max over tensor occupation measures of a relative entropy; for weakly irreducible T the maximizer is explicit in u, w.

conclusions: Then $\mu$ is an occupation measure whose support is $\supp \mathcal{T}$.

Let $\mathcal{J}_{n,d}\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{	imes d}}$ be a symmetric tensor whose all entries are $1$. For a positive integer $l$ let $\mathcal{T}_l=\mathcal{T}+ rac{1}{l} \mathcal{J}_{n,d}$. Then $\mathcal{T}_l$ is weakly irreducible. Our arguments yield that there exists positive occupation measure $\mu(l)=[\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}(l)]\in\Omega(n^{	imes (d-1)})$ such that \[\logho(\mathcal{T}_l)=\sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d\in [n]} \mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d}(l) \log \Big( rac{(\sum_{k_2,\dots, k_d}\mu_{i_1,k_2,\dots, k_d}(l))(t_{i_1,\dots, i_d}+ rac{1}{l})}{\mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d}(l)}\Big) \enspace .\] As $\Omega(n^{	imes (d-1)})$ is a compact set, there is a subsequence of $\{\mu(l)\},l\in \mathbb{N}$ which converges to the occupation measure $\mu\in\Omega(n^{	imes (d-1)})$. Hence \[\logho(\mathcal{T})=\sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d\in [n]} \mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d} \log \Big( rac{(\sum_{k_2,\dots, k_d}\mu_{i_1,k_2,\dots, k_d})t_{i_1,\dots, i_d}}{\mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d}}\Big) \enspace .\] Combine this equality with the inequality \eqref{baslogrineqten} to deduce the theorem in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Analogue of the matrix proof: convexity of t -> log rho(nu o e^{tB}) with the first variation formula gives the bound. Approximation T + J/l and compactness of the occupation measures handle the reducible case.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Analogy with the matrix case
nodes.statement: The proof of this theorem is analogous to the proof of Theorem \ref{AGchar} and we repeat briefly the analogous arguments.
nodes.statement_short: The proof follows that of Theorem 17.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Normalize mu to a stochastic tensor nu
nodes.statement:
Fix a weakly irreducible tensor $\mathcal{T}=[t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{	imes d}}$. Assume that $\mu=[\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in \Omega(n^{	imes(d-1)})$ has the same support as $\mathcal{T}$. Let $
u=[
u_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{	imes d}}$ be the following weakly irreducible tensor \[
u_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}= rac{\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}}{x_{i_1}}, \;x_{i_1}={\sum_{j_2,\ldots,j_d\in[n]}\mu_{i_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d}}, \quad i_1,\ldots,i_d\in[n].\] Let $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^	op $ Since $\mu$ is a weakly irreducible tensor and an occupation measure if follows that $\mathbf{x}$ is a positive probability vector.
nodes.statement_short: From mu with the support of T build nu with row sums x.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Perron data of nu
nodes.statement:
Clearly $
u\otimes^{d-1}\mathbf{1}_n=\mathbf{1}_n$. Hence $ho(
u)=1$ and the corresponding eigenvector is $\mathbf{1}_n$. Recall that $D
u(\mathbf{x})=(d-1) 
u	imes \otimes^{d-2} \mathbf{x}$ (\eqref{partderT}). Hence, the entries for the matrix $A(\mu)=(d-1)D
u(\mathbf{1}_n)=[a_{ij}]\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n	imes n}$, defined in \eqref{defATu} , are given by \[a_{ij}= rac{d-1}{x_i}\sum_{i_3,\cdots,i_d\in[n]}\mu_{i,j,i_3,\cdots,i_d}, \quad i,j\in[n].\] Since $\mu$ is an occupation measure it follows that $\mathbf{x}^	op A(\mu)=\mathbf{x}^	op$ \[\sum_{i=1}^n x_i a_{ij}=(d-1)\sum_{i,i_3,\cdots,i_d\in[n]}\mu_{i,j,i_3,\cdots,i_d}=x_j \; orall j\in[n].\]
nodes.statement_short: rho(nu) = 1 with eigenvector 1, and x is left-invariant for A(mu).
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Convexity bound
nodes.statement_short: Log-convexity and the first variation formula give (6.10).
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Basic entropy inequality for tensors (6.10)
nodes.statement: \log\rho(\mathcal{T})\geqslant \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_d\in[n]}\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}\log\frac{t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}\sum_{j_2,\ldots,j_d\in[n]} \mu_{i_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d}}{\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}}.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor
nodes.label: baslogrineqten

nodes.name: Extend the bound to all mu
nodes.statement: The density argument yields that the above inequality holds for any $\mu\in\Omega(n^{\times(d-1)},\supp \mathcal{T})$. Let $\mu\in\Omega(n^{\times(d-1)})$ and assume that $\supp \mu$ is not contained in $\supp \mathcal{T}$. Hence there exists a positive entry of $\mu$: $\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}$ such that $t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}=0$. Therefore \[\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}\log\frac{t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}\sum_{j_2,\ldots,j_d\in[n]} \mu_{i_1,j_2,\ldots,j_d}}{\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}}=-\infty.\] In this case \eqref{baslogrineqten} trivially holds. These arguments show that $\log\rho(\mathcal{T})$ is not less that the right-hand side of \eqref{entropcharsrten1}.
nodes.statement_short: Density and the -infinity convention extend the upper bound to all occupation measures.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Optimal occupation measure
nodes.statement: Let $\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n^{\times d}}$ be given by \eqref{mumaxten}. As $\mathcal{T}$ is partially symmetric it follows that $\mu$ is partially symmetric. As $\mathbf{u}$ is an eigenvector of $\mathcal{T}$ corresponding to $\rho(\mathcal{T})$ we deduce that \[\sum_{i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]} \mu_{j,i_2,\ldots,i_d}=w_j u_{j}^{-(d-2)}u_j^{d-1}=w_j u_j \; \forall j\in [n].\] As $\mathbf{w}^\top\mathbf{u}=1$ it follows that $\mu$ is a probability tensor. Let $A(\mathcal{T})$ be defined as in \eqref{defATu}. Since $\mathbf{w}^\top A(\mathcal{T})=(d-1)\rho(\mathcal{T})\mathbf{w}^\top$, (the second equality in \eqref{defpropA}), it follows that $\mu$ satisfies \eqref{tenocmeas}. The equality \eqref{logeqtenT} is deduced in a similar way the equality in Lemma \ref{auxlemAG}.
nodes.statement_short: The measure (6.8) is an occupation measure attaining (6.9).
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Not weakly irreducible, rho = 0
nodes.statement: Assume now that $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$ is not weakly irreducible. As in the proof of Theorem \ref{AGchar} it follows that the inequality \eqref{baslogrineqten} holds. Suppose first that $\rho(\mathcal{T})=0$. Then $\log\rho(\mathcal{T})=-\infty$. Hence \eqref{entropcharsrten1} trivially holds. Equivalently, for each $\mu\in\Omega(n^{\times (d-1)})$ there exists $i_1,\ldots,i_d\in[n]$ such that $\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}>0$ and $t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Not weakly irreducible: the inequality still holds; rho = 0 is trivial.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Not weakly irreducible, rho > 0
nodes.statement: Assume now that $\rho(\mathcal{T})>0$. Let $\mathcal{J}_{n,d}\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$ be a symmetric tensor whose all entries are $1$. For a positive integer $l$ let $\mathcal{T}_l=\mathcal{T}+\frac{1}{l} \mathcal{J}_{n,d}$. Then $\mathcal{T}_l$ is weakly irreducible. Our arguments yield that there exists positive occupation measure $\mu(l)=[\mu_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}(l)]\in\Omega(n^{\times (d-1)})$ such that \[\log\rho(\mathcal{T}_l)=\sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d\in [n]} \mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d}(l) \log \Big(\frac{(\sum_{k_2,\dots, k_d}\mu_{i_1,k_2,\dots, k_d}(l))(t_{i_1,\dots, i_d}+\frac{1}{l})}{\mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d}(l)}\Big) \enspace .\] As $\Omega(n^{\times (d-1)})$ is a compact set, there is a subsequence of $\{\mu(l)\},l\in \mathbb{N}$ which converges to the occupation measure $\mu\in\Omega(n^{\times (d-1)})$. Hence \[\log\rho(\mathcal{T})=\sum_{i_1,\dots,i_d\in [n]} \mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d} \log \Big(\frac{(\sum_{k_2,\dots, k_d}\mu_{i_1,k_2,\dots, k_d})t_{i_1,\dots, i_d}}{\mu_{i_1,\dots, i_d}}\Big) \enspace .\] Combine this equality with the inequality \eqref{baslogrineqten} to deduce the theorem in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate by T + J/l and use compactness of the occupation measures.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Concavity of the relative entropy objective
nodes.statement: The function which is maximized in~\eqref{entropcharsrten1} is a relative entropy. This function is known to be concave; this follows from the fact that the perspective function of a convex function is convex, see~\cite[\S~3.2.6]{boyd}, and also~\cite{CS16}.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Log-convexity recovered from the entropic formula
nodes.statement: The log-convexity of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor, Corollary~\ref{logconvsr}, can be recovered from Theorem~\ref{entropcharsrten}, as formula~\eqref{entropcharsrten1} shows that the logarithm of the spectral radius, which is a maximum of linear functions of the logarithms of the entries of the tensor, is a convex function of these logarithms.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor

nodes.name: Ergodic control interpretation for tensors
nodes.statement: The ergodic control interpretation of the logarithm of the spectral radius, explained in \Cref{subsec-ergodic}, extends to the case of nonnegative tensors. The set of actions of the player is still the finite set $[n]$. The set of actions in state $i$ consists of probability measures $p=(p_{i,i_2,\dots,i_n})_{i_2,\dots,i_n}$ on the set $S_i:= \{(i_2,\dots,i_d)\in [n]^d\mid a_{i,i_2,\dots,i_n}>0$. If an action $p$ is selected, the next state becomes $j$ with probability $\sum_{2\leqslant k\leqslant n,\;\; i_k = j} p_{i,i_2,\dots,i_n}$. Then, the player receives the payment \[ \operatorname{KL}_i(p,\mathcal{T})= -\sum_{(j_2,\dots,j_d)\in S_i} p_{i,i_2,\dots,i_d}\log(p_{i,i_2,\dots,i_d}/t_{i,i_2,\dots,i_d}) \enspace. \] We leave it to the reader to check, arguing as in \Cref{subsec-ergodic}, that the value of the associated ergodic game is independent of the initial state as soon as $\mathcal{T}$ is weakly irreducible, and that Formula~\eqref{logeqtenT} allows us to identify $\log \rho(\mathcal{T})$ to the value of this game.
nodes.statement_short: log rho(T) is the value of a one-player ergodic game with simplex action spaces and Kullback-Leibler payments.
nodes.section: 6.3 Entropic characterization of the spectral radius of a nonnegative tensor
nodes.label: rem-ergodiccontrol

nodes.name: l_p norm
nodes.statement: Given $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^\top \in \mathbb{C}^{n}$, we set $\|\mathbf{x}\|_p:=(\sum_{i=1}^n |x_i|^p)^{\frac{1}{p}}$, for $p\in (0,\infty]$.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Karlin-Ost monotonicity for tensors
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$. Then the function $s\mapsto \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}$ is nonincreasing on $(0,\infty)$.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
conclusions: the function $s\mapsto \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}$ is nonincreasing on $(0,\infty)$
nodes.label: genKO

nodes.name: Proof of Karlin-Ost monotonicity
nodes.statement: It is enough to show that \begin{equation} \rho(\mathcal{T})\geqslant \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}} \textrm{ for } s>1. \end{equation} As in the proof of Lemma \ref{genkinin} we may assume that $\mathcal{T}$ is weakly irreducible. Let $\mathbf{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_n)^\top>\mathbf{0}$ be the eigenvector of $\mathcal{T}$ satisfying \eqref{poseigvec}. Use the well known fact that $\|\mathbf{x}\|_p$ is a nonincreasing function of $p$ to deduce that \[\rho(\mathcal{T})u_i^{d-1}=\mathcal{T}(\mathbf{u})_i\geqslant (\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{u}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}} \textrm{ for } i\in [n] \Rightarrow \mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{u}^{\circ s})\leqslant \rho(\mathcal{T})^s (\mathbf{u}^{\circ s})^{d-1}.\] Use characterization \eqref{infmaxcharrho} to deduce \eqref{spowin}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to s>1 and weak irreducibility; monotonicity of l_p norms plus Collatz-Wielandt.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Reduce to s > 1
nodes.statement: It is enough to show that \begin{equation} \rho(\mathcal{T})\geqslant \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}} \textrm{ for } s>1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to prove (7.1) for s > 1.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Power inequality (7.1)
nodes.statement: \rho(\mathcal{T})\geqslant \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}} \textrm{ for } s>1.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: spowin

nodes.name: Reduce to weakly irreducible
nodes.statement: As in the proof of Lemma \ref{genkinin} we may assume that $\mathcal{T}$ is weakly irreducible. Let $\mathbf{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_n)^\top>\mathbf{0}$ be the eigenvector of $\mathcal{T}$ satisfying \eqref{poseigvec}.
nodes.statement_short: Assume weak irreducibility and take the Perron eigenvector u.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Monotonicity of l_p norms
nodes.statement: Use the well known fact that $\|\mathbf{x}\|_p$ is a nonincreasing function of $p$ to deduce that \[\rho(\mathcal{T})u_i^{d-1}=\mathcal{T}(\mathbf{u})_i\geqslant (\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{u}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}} \textrm{ for } i\in [n] \Rightarrow \mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{u}^{\circ s})\leqslant \rho(\mathcal{T})^s (\mathbf{u}^{\circ s})^{d-1}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of l_p norms bounds T^{os}(u^{os}).
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Collatz-Wielandt
nodes.statement: Use characterization \eqref{infmaxcharrho} to deduce \eqref{spowin}.
nodes.statement_short: Collatz-Wielandt gives (7.1).
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Proof of the strengthened Hadamard inequality
nodes.statement: Combine the above theorem with \eqref{genkinin1} to give a stronger version of \eqref{specradcircin}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Karlin-Ost monotonicity with the generalized Kingman inequality.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Strengthened Hadamard product inequality
nodes.statement: \rho(\mathcal{T}\circ\mathcal{S})\leqslant \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ \frac{1}{2}}\circ\mathcal{S}^{\circ \frac{1}{2}})^2\leqslant \rho(\mathcal{T})\rho(\mathcal{S}), \quad \mathcal{S},\mathcal{T}\in \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: specradcircinsv

nodes.name: Tropical eigenvector and eigenvalue
nodes.statement: We say that a nonzero nonnegative vector $u$ is a \emph{tropical eigenvector} of the tensor $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$, with the associated \emph{tropical eigenvalue} $\lambda$ if \[ \max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}u_{i_2}\ldots u_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\} = \lambda u_i^{d-1} \enspace,\qquad i\in [n] . \]
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Existence of tropical eigenvectors
nodes.statement: The existence of a tropical eigenvector $u$ follows from a standard application of Brouwer's theorem.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
conclusions: The existence of a tropical eigenvector $u$

nodes.name: Bound on the number of tropical eigenvalues
nodes.statement: Moreover, the number of distinct tropical eigenvalues is bounded by $2^n-1$, this follows e.g.\ from~\cite[Th.~5.2.3]{nussbaumlemmens}.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
conclusions: the number of distinct tropical eigenvalues is bounded by $2^n-1$

nodes.name: Tropical spectral radius
nodes.statement: The \emph{tropical spectral radius} of $\mathcal{T}$, denoted by $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$, is defined as the maximal tropical eigenvalue of $\mathcal{T}$.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Limit eigenvalue rho_infty
nodes.statement: We shall also consider the limit eigenvalue: \begin{equation} \rho_{\infty}(\mathcal{T}):=\lim_{s\to\infty} \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Limit eigenvalue (7.3)
nodes.statement: \rho_{\infty}(\mathcal{T}):=\lim_{s\to\infty} \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: tropspecrad

nodes.name: Collatz-Wielandt characterization of the tropical spectral radius
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}\in \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$. Then \begin{equation} \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})=\inf_{\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^\top>0} \max_{i\in[n]} \frac{\max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}x_{i_2}\ldots x_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\}}{x_i^{d-1}}. \end{equation} There exists a tropical eigenvector $\mathbf{v}=(v_1,\ldots,v_n) ^\top \gneq \mathbf{0}$ corresponding to $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$ \begin{equation} \max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}v_{i_2}\ldots v_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\}=\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})v_i^{d-1} \textrm{ for } i\in [n]. \end{equation} Assume that $\mathcal{T}$ is irreducible. Then every eigenvector $\mathbf{v}$ satisfying \eqref{tropspeceig} is positive. Assume that $\mathcal{T}$ is weakly irreducible. Then, there exists a positive eigenvector $\mathbf{v}$ satisfying \eqref{tropspeceig}, and in the characterization \eqref{tropspecradchar}, the infimum can be replaced by the minimum.
nodes.statement_short: Collatz-Wielandt inf-max formula for rho_trop, existence of a nonnegative tropical eigenvector, positivity under (weak) irreducibility.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
conclusions: There exists a tropical eigenvector $\mathbf{v}=(v_1,\ldots,v_n) ^\top \gneq \mathbf{0}$ corresponding to $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$
in the characterization \eqref{tropspecradchar}, the infimum can be replaced by the minimum
There exists a tropical eigenvector $\mathbf{v}=(v_1,\ldots,v_n) ^\top \gneq \mathbf{0}$ corresponding to $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$
in the characterization \eqref{tropspecradchar}, the infimum can be replaced by the minimum

nodes.label: tropspecradthm0

nodes.name: Tropical Collatz-Wielandt formula (7.4)
nodes.statement: \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})=\inf_{\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^\top>0} \max_{i\in[n]} \frac{\max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}x_{i_2}\ldots x_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\}}{x_i^{d-1}}.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: tropspecradchar

nodes.name: Tropical eigenvector equation (7.5)
nodes.statement: \max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}v_{i_2}\ldots v_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\}=\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})v_i^{d-1} \textrm{ for } i\in [n].
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: tropspeceig

nodes.name: Proof of the tropical Collatz-Wielandt theorem
nodes.statement: Formula~\eqref{tropspecradchar} follows from the Collatz-Wielandt characterization of the spectral radius of a non-linear map~\cite{nuss86}. The existence of a positive eigenvector, if $\mathcal{T}$ is weakly irreducible, follows from the generalized Perron-Frobenius theorem~\cite[Theorem 2]{GG04}. When $\mathcal{T}$ is irreducible, it is straightforward to check that any nonnegative eigenvector must be positive.
nodes.statement_short: Collatz-Wielandt for nonlinear maps (Nussbaum) and the generalized Perron-Frobenius theorem (Gaubert-Gunawardena).
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Collatz-Wielandt for nonlinear maps
nodes.statement: Formula~\eqref{tropspecradchar} follows from the Collatz-Wielandt characterization of the spectral radius of a non-linear map~\cite{nuss86}.
nodes.statement_short: Formula (7.4) from Nussbaum's Collatz-Wielandt theorem.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Generalized Perron-Frobenius
nodes.statement: The existence of a positive eigenvector, if $\mathcal{T}$ is weakly irreducible, follows from the generalized Perron-Frobenius theorem~\cite[Theorem 2]{GG04}. When $\mathcal{T}$ is irreducible, it is straightforward to check that any nonnegative eigenvector must be positive.
nodes.statement_short: Positive eigenvector from Gaubert-Gunawardena; positivity for irreducible T is direct.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Irreducible case previously known
nodes.statement: The special case of~\Cref{tropspecradthm0} concerning irreducible tensors was proved in \cite[Th~3.3]{BUSH201964}.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Lower bound by the tropical spectral radius
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}\in \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$. Then for $s>0$ the following inequality hold. \[ \rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}\geqslant \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T}) \enspace . \]
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: coro-lower

nodes.name: Proof of the tropical lower bound
nodes.statement: {{The characterization \eqref{infmaxcharrho} yields the Collatz-Wielandt characterization of $\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}$ for a positive $s>0$: \[\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}= \inf_{\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^\top>\mathbf{0}}\max_{i\in[n]} \frac{(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{x}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}}}{x_i^{d-1}}.\] Clearly, \begin{eqnarray*} \max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}x_{i_2}\ldots x_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\}\leqslant (\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{x}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}}, \quad i\in[n]. \end{eqnarray*} Compare the Collatz-Wielandt characterizations of $\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$, given by \eqref{tropspecradchar}, to deduce the lemma.}}
nodes.statement_short: Compare the Collatz-Wielandt formulas for rho(T^{os})^{1/s} and rho_trop termwise.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Collatz-Wielandt for Hadamard powers
nodes.statement: {{The characterization \eqref{infmaxcharrho} yields the Collatz-Wielandt characterization of $\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}$ for a positive $s>0$: \[\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}= \inf_{\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^\top>\mathbf{0}}\max_{i\in[n]} \frac{(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{x}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}}}{x_i^{d-1}}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Collatz-Wielandt formula for rho(T^{os})^{1/s}.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Termwise max bound
nodes.statement: Clearly, \begin{eqnarray*} \max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}x_{i_2}\ldots x_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\}\leqslant (\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{x}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}}, \quad i\in[n]. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Max of terms is at most their l_s norm.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Termwise max bound
nodes.statement: \max\{t_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}x_{i_2}\ldots x_{i_d},\;i_2,\ldots,i_d\in[n]\}\leqslant (\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{x}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}}, \quad i\in[n].
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: basintropchar

nodes.name: Compare characterizations
nodes.statement: Compare the Collatz-Wielandt characterizations of $\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$, given by \eqref{tropspecradchar}, to deduce the lemma.}}
nodes.statement_short: Compare with (7.4).
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Tropical spectral radius equals limit eigenvalue
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}\in \mathbb{R}_{ps,+}^{n^{\times d}}$. Then \[ \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T}) = \rho_\infty(\mathcal{T}) \enspace . \]
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: tropspecradthm

nodes.name: Proof that rho_trop = rho_infty
nodes.statement: {{In the inequality given by Proposition \eqref{coro-lower}, let $s\to\infty$ to obtain $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})\leqslant \rho_{\infty}(\mathcal{T})$. Assume that $\mathbf{x}>\mathbf{0}$. The Collatz-Wielandt characterization of $\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}$ yields that $\rho(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s})^{\frac{1}{s}}\leqslant \max_{i\in[n]} \frac{(\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}(\mathbf{x}^{\circ s})_i)^{\frac{1}{s}}}{x_i^{d-1}}$. With each $d-1$ cycle $\gamma$ associate the following weighted average of the entries of $\mathcal{F}$ along $\gamma$. \begin{equation} w(\gamma,\mathcal{F})=(\prod_{v\in V(\gamma)} f_{v,j_2(v,\gamma),\ldots,j_d(v,\gamma)})^{u(\gamma)_v}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of the combinatorial characterization
nodes.statement: Assume first that $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F})>0$. Let $V'\subset [n]$ will be the smallest subset of indices for which the coordinate $v_i$ of the tropical eigenvector $\mathbf{v}$ satisfying \eqref{tropspeceig} with the following restriction. For each $i\in V'$ $v_i>0$ and the corresponding maximum in \eqref{tropspeceig} can be taken only on $i_2,\ldots,i_d\in V'$. For each $k\in V'$, we choose indices $i_2=j_2(k),\ldots,i_d=j_d(k)\in V'$ achieving the maximum in \eqref{tropspeceig}, so that \begin{equation} t_{i,j_2(i),\ldots,j_d(i)} v_{j_2(i)}\ldots v_{j_d(i)} = \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T}) v_i^{d-1}, \qquad i\in V'. \end{equation} This defines a digraph $\gamma$. The minimality of $V'$ implies that $\gamma\in\Sigma_{n,d-1}$ is a $(d-1)$-dicycle. Let $\mathbf{u}(\gamma)$ be defined from $\gamma$, as in~\eqref{defleAgam}. We now raise each term of the $i$th equality~\eqref{eq-saturate} to the power $u(\gamma)_i$, \begin{equation} (t_{i,j_2(i),\ldots,j_d(i)} v_{j_2(i)}\ldots v_{j_d(i)} )^{u(\gamma)_i} = (\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})v_i^{d-1})^{u(\gamma)_i}, \qquad i \in V' \enspace . \end{equation} We next multiply all the equalities~\eqref{e-saturate2}, and observe that, thanks to~\eqref{defleAgam}, the terms involving powers of $v$ can be canceled, showing that \[ \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F})= w(\gamma,\mathcal{F}) \leqslant \max_{\gamma'\in\Sigma_{n,d-1}} w(\gamma',\mathcal{F}) \enspace.\] We show the reverse inequality. Given $\gamma\in \Sigma_{n,d-1}$ let $\mathcal{F}(\gamma)=[f(\gamma)_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]$ be the following symmetric tensor in the last $d-1$ indices: $f(\gamma)_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}=f_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}$ if an only if $i\in V(\gamma)$ and $(i_2,\ldots,i_d)$ are permutations of $(j_2(i,\gamma), \ldots,j_d(i,\gamma)$. Otherwise $f_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}=0$. Clearly, $\mathcal{F}(\gamma)\leqslant \mathcal{F}$. Hence $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F}(\gamma))\leqslant \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F})$. Arguing as in the first part of the proof, we show that $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F}(\gamma))=w(\gamma,\mathcal{F})$. Hence we have characterization \eqref{chartropeigten1}. The above arguments show that $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F})=0$ if and only if each $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F}(\gamma))=0$ for each $\gamma\in\Sigma_{n,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Saturating indices of a tropical eigenvector form a (d-1)-cycle whose weight equals rho_trop; conversely restrict F to a cycle.

nodes.name: Positive case: minimal support
nodes.statement: Assume first that $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F})>0$. Let $V'\subset [n]$ will be the smallest subset of indices for which the coordinate $v_i$ of the tropical eigenvector $\mathbf{v}$ satisfying \eqref{tropspeceig} with the following restriction. For each $i\in V'$ $v_i>0$ and the corresponding maximum in \eqref{tropspeceig} can be taken only on $i_2,\ldots,i_d\in V'$.

nodes.name: Saturating indices

nodes.name: The saturation digraph is a cycle
nodes.statement: This defines a digraph $\gamma$. The minimality of $V'$ implies that $\gamma\in\Sigma_{n,d-1}$ is a $(d-1)$-dicycle. Let $\mathbf{u}(\gamma)$ be defined from $\gamma$, as in~\eqref{defleAgam}.

nodes.name: Raise to invariant-measure powers
nodes.statement: We now raise each term of the $i$th equality~\eqref{eq-saturate} to the power $u(\gamma)_i$, \begin{equation} (t_{i,j_2(i),\ldots,j_d(i)} v_{j_2(i)}\ldots v_{j_d(i)} )^{u(\gamma)_i} = (\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})v_i^{d-1})^{u(\gamma)_i}, \qquad i \in V' \enspace . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Multiply and cancel

nodes.name: Reverse inequality
nodes.statement: We show the reverse inequality. Given $\gamma\in \Sigma_{n,d-1}$ let $\mathcal{F}(\gamma)=[f(\gamma)_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]$ be the following symmetric tensor in the last $d-1$ indices: $f(\gamma)_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}=f_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}$ if an only if $i\in V(\gamma)$ and $(i_2,\ldots,i_d)$ are permutations of $(j_2(i,\gamma), \ldots,j_d(i,\gamma)$. Otherwise $f_{i,i_2,\ldots,i_d}=0$. Clearly, $\mathcal{F}(\gamma)\leqslant \mathcal{F}$. Hence $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F}(\gamma))\leqslant \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F})$. Arguing as in the first part of the proof, we show that $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{F}(\gamma))=w(\gamma,\mathcal{F})$. Hence we have characterization \eqref{chartropeigten1}.

nodes.name: Zero case

nodes.name: Concise support encoding S-bar(T)
nodes.statement: Since the tensor $\mathcal{T}$ is supposed to be symmetric in the indices $i_2,\dots,i_d$, for computational purposes, we will use a concise encoding of the support, $\bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})\subset \supp \mathcal{T}$, so that $\bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})$ contains precisely one element $(i_1,i_2,\dots,i_d)$ in each symmetry class $\{(i_1,\sigma(i_2),\dots,\sigma(i_d))\mid \sigma\in S_{d-1}\}$, where $S_{d-1}$ denotes the symmetric group on $d-1$ symbols.

nodes.name: Linear programming formulation of the tropical spectral radius
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}=[t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in\mathbb{R}_{ps.+}^{n^{\times d}}$. Then, $\log\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$ coincides with the value of the following linear program \begin{eqnarray} \min \lambda,& \lambda \in \mathbb{R}, \qquad u\in \mathbb{R}^n &\nonumber \\ \log t_{i_1,\dots,i_d} + u_{i_1} + \dots +u_{i_d} &\leqslant \lambda + (d-1) u_{i_1} , \qquad \forall (i_1,\dots,i_d) \in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T}) \enspace . \end{eqnarray} In particular, $\log\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$ can be computed in polynomial time in the Turing model of computation, assuming that the input consists of the set $\bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})$ and of numbers $\log t_{i_1,\dots,i_d} \in \mathbb{Q}$ for $(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})$.\hfill\qed
nodes.statement_short: log rho_trop(T) is the value of an explicit LP, hence computable in polynomial time.

nodes.name: LP constraints (7.20)
nodes.statement: \min \lambda,& \lambda \in \mathbb{R}, \qquad u\in \mathbb{R}^n &\nonumber \\ \log t_{i_1,\dots,i_d} + u_{i_1} + \dots +u_{i_d} &\leqslant \lambda + (d-1) u_{i_1} , \qquad \forall (i_1,\dots,i_d) \in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T}) \enspace .
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: e-ineqlp

nodes.name: Proof of the dual LP formulation
nodes.statement: It follows from the strong duality theorem in linear programming that the value of the linear program in Corollary~\ref{cor-lp} coincides with the one of its dual. By computing the dual linear program, we obtain the following consequence of Corollary~\ref{cor-lp}, in which $\mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d}$ denotes the Lagrange multiplier of the inequality constraint~\eqref{e-ineqlp}.
nodes.statement_short: LP strong duality applied to Corollary 27.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Dual linear program for the tropical spectral radius
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}=[t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in\mathbb{R}_{ps.+}^{n^{\times d}}$. Then, $\log\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$ coincides with the value of the following linear program \begin{eqnarray*} \max \sum_{(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})} \mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d} \log t_{i_1,\dots i_d,} \nonumber\\ \mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d}\geqslant 0, & \text{for } (i_1,\dots,i_d)\in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})\nonumber\\ \sum_{(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})\atop i_1=j} \mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d} &= \displaystyle\sum_{(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})\atop j=i_2,\dots,i_d } \mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d} \qquad \forall j\in [n]\enspace ,\\ \sum_{(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})} \mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d} &=1 \end{eqnarray*} \hfill\qed
nodes.statement_short: log rho_trop(T) is the value of a max-entropy-free LP over occupation measures supported on S-bar(T).
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
conclusions: $\log\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T})$ coincides with the value of the following linear program
nodes.label: cor-lp2

nodes.name: Proof of tropical log-convexity
nodes.statement: The next corollary follows from~\eqref{chartropeigten1}.
nodes.statement_short: Each cycle weight is a product of entries to fixed powers, hence logconvex; a max of logconvex functions is logconvex.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Log-convexity of the tropical spectral radius
nodes.statement: Let $D\subset \mathbb{R}^m$ be a convex set. Assume that $\mathcal{T}:D\to \mathbb{R}_+^{n^{\times d}}$ is logconvex. Then $\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}(\mathcal{T}):D\to\mathbb{R}_+$ is logconvex. \hfill\qed
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: logconvtrop

nodes.name: Tropical spectral radius as value of an ergodic MDP
nodes.statement: It follows from the above linear programming formulations that $\log\rho_{\mathrm{trop}}$ coincides with the value of an ergodic Markov decision process (MDP), i.e., a one player stochastic game with mean payoff~\cite{whittle86}, in which the state space is $[n]$. This game appears to be ``a degeneration'' of the game with entropic payment in Remark~\ref{rem-ergodiccontrol}, in which now, the action spaces become finite. Let us describe this MDP. In a given state $j$, the set of actions consists of $\{(j,i_2,\dots,i_d)\in \bar{\mathcal{S}}(\mathcal{T})\}$, the player receives the payment $\log t_{j,i_2,\dots ,i_d}$, the next state become $k$ with probability $|\{2\leqslant \ell\leqslant d\mid i_\ell =k\}|/(d-1)$, and $\log \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}$ represents the best mean payoff per time unit. Then, the digraphs $\gamma$ arising in the combinatorial characterization~\eqref{chartropeigten1} correspond to feedback policies, and this characterization shows that $\log \rho_{\mathrm{trop}}$ is the supremum of the ergodic payments attached to the different feedback policies, a general property of ergodic Markov decision processes~\cite[Prop.~7.2]{AG03}. The dual variables $\mu_{i_1,\dots,i_d}$ represent an {\em occupation measure}, giving the frequency at which an action $(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ is played.
nodes.statement_short: log rho_trop is the mean-payoff value of a finite-action MDP, a degeneration of the entropic game; cycles are feedback policies.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Tropical eigenproblem for n=2, d=4
nodes.statement: Take $n=2$ and $d=4$. Then, the general tropical eigenproblem can be written as follows, \begin{eqnarray} \lambda v_1^3 & =& \max(t_{1111}v_1^3,\, t_{1112}v_1^2v_2, \, t_{1122}v_1v_2^2,\, t_{1222}v_2^3) \\ \lambda v_2^3 &=& \max(t_{2111}v_1^3,\, t_{2112}v_1^2v_2, \, t_{2122}v_1v_2^2,\, t_{2222}v_2^3) \enspace . \end{eqnarray} We suppose here, without loss of generality, that the tensor is symmetric in the last $3$ indices. We next list the different cycles appearing in the representation of \Cref{chartropeigten}. First, there are two $3$-cycles with vertex set of cardinality $1$ (multiloops). The first of these $3-$cycles arises by considering the multigraph $\gamma^1_1$, with vertex set $V_1^1=\{1\}$ and edges multiset $E^1_1=\{(1,1), (1,1),(1,1)\}$, meaning that edge $(1,1)$ is repeated $3$ times. Then, the adjacency matrix $A(\gamma^1_1)$ is the $1\times 1$ matrix equal to $(3)$, the associated invariant measure $u(\gamma^1_1)$ is the one-dimensional vector $(1)$, leading to the weight \begin{equation} w(\gamma^1_1) =t_{1111} \enspace . \end{equation} Similarly, there is another $3$-cycle $\gamma^1_2$ with vertex set of cardinality $1$, namely $V^1_2=\{2\}$, with edge multiset $E^1_2=\{(2,2),(2,2),(2,2)\}$, leading to the weight \begin{equation} w(\gamma^1_2) =t_{2222} \enspace . \end{equation} Less trivial examples arise when considering $3$-cycles with vertex set of cardinality $2$, like $\gamma_1^2$, with vertex set $V^2_1=\{1,2\}$ and edge multiset $E^2_1=\{(1,1),(1,1), (1,2), (2,1)$, $(2,1),(2,1)\}$. The associated adjacency matrix is \[ A(\gamma_1^2)= \left(\begin{array}{cc} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 \end{array}\right) \] with invariant measure $u(\gamma^2_1)= (3/4,1/4)$, leading to the weight \begin{equation} w(\gamma_1^2)= t_{1112}^{3/4}t_{2111}^{1/4} \enspace . \end{equation} This suggests the following rule to construct all the $3$-cycles with a vertex set of cardinality $2$: -- in state $1$, select one of the terms at the right hand side of~\eqref{e-eq-t1} except the first term $t_{1111}v_1^3$ (which would lead to a multiloop), --- in state $2$, select one of the terms at the right hand side of~\eqref{e-eq-t2}, except the first term $t_{2222}v_2^3$; Then, the exponents of the terms which are selected determine the edges of the multigraph. For instance, selecting $t_{1112}v_1^2v_2$ in state $1$, and $t_{2111}v_1^3$ in state $2$, yields the exponent vectors $(2,1)$ and $(3,0)$, corresponding precisely to the rows of the matrix $A(\gamma_1^2)$. It follows that there are precisely $9$ $3$-cycles not reduced to multiloops, corresponding to these different selections. We next list the adjacency matrices of all these $3$-cycles, and the associated weights, \begin{eqnarray*} \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c} \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right) & \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{smallmatrix}\right)\\ &&&&&&&\\ \scriptstyle t_{1112}^{3/4}t_{2111}^{1/4}& \scriptstyle t_{1112}^{2/3}t_{2112}^{1/3}& \scriptstyle t_{1112}^{1/2}t_{2122}^{1/2}& \scriptstyle t_{1122}^{3/5}t_{2111}^{2/5}& \scriptstyle t_{1122}^{1/2}t_{2112}^{1/2}& \scriptstyle t_{1122}^{1/3}t_{2122}^{2/3}& \scriptstyle t_{1222}^{1/2}t_{2111}^{1/2}& \scriptstyle t_{1222}^{2/5}t_{2112}^{3/5}& \scriptstyle t_{1222}^{1/4}t_{2122}^{3/4} \end{array} \end{eqnarray*} \Cref{chartropeigten} shows that the tropical spectral radius of $\mathcal{T}$ is given by the maximum of the weights~\eqref{e-gamma1}, \eqref{e-gamma2new} and of the weights appearing in the latter table.
nodes.statement_short: Lists all 3-cycles for n=2, d=4 and their weights; rho_trop is the maximum of these weights.

nodes.name: Algorithms for the tropical spectral radius
nodes.statement: Corollary~\ref{cor-lp} leads to a polynomial time algorithm to compute the spectral radius of a tropical tensor. The reduction to ergodic Markov decision processes allows us, more generally, to apply any algorithm developed in this setting, including policy iteration~\cite{whittle86}. For huge scale instances, iterative power type algorithms may be more suitable. One may use the relative value iteration~\cite{white}. This algorithm does converge if the optimal strategies satisfy a certain cyclicity condition (Corollary~5.9 and Theorem 6.6 of \cite{AG03}). One can also use the projective Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration described in~\cite{Gstott}, section 5, which is a power type algorithm with damping that converges without any condition of cyclicity.
nodes.statement_short: LP gives a polynomial algorithm; policy iteration, relative value iteration or Krasnoselskii-Mann iterations also apply.
nodes.section: 7 Tropical spectral radius of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Spectral norm of a tensor
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}$. Recall the definition of the spectral norm of $\mathcal{T}$, see~\cite{FL17}, \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}=\max\{|\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j)|, \;\|\mathbf{x}_j\|=1, j\in[d]\}, \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Spectral norm (8.1)
nodes.statement: \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}=\max\{|\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j)|, \;\|\mathbf{x}_j\|=1, j\in[d]\},
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: defspecnrm

nodes.name: Spectral radius bounded by spectral norm
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{C}^{n^{\times d}}_{ps}$. Then \begin{equation} \rho(\mathcal{T})\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}n^{(d-2)/2}. \end{equation}

nodes.label: specneqrad

nodes.name: Spectral radius vs spectral norm (8.2)
nodes.statement: \rho(\mathcal{T})\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}n^{(d-2)/2}.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: specneqrad1

nodes.name: Proof of the spectral norm bound
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathcal{T}\times (\otimes^{d-1}\mathbf{x})=\lambda \mathbf{x}^{(d-1)}$ and $|\lambda|=\rho(\mathcal{T})$. Normalize $\mathbf{x}$ by $\|\mathbf{x}^{(d-1)}\|=1$. Let $\mathbf{y}=\bar{\mathbf{x}}^{(d-1)}$, the complex conjugate of $\mathbf{x}^{(d-1)}$, so that $\|\mathbf{y}\|=1$. Then $|\mathcal{T}\times(\mathbf{y}\otimes(\otimes^{d-1}\mathbf{x})|= |\lambda|$. Therefore $|\lambda|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\|\mathbf{y}\|\|\mathbf{x}\|^{d-1}=\|\mathcal{T}\|_\infty \|\mathbf{x}\|^{d-1}$. Use H\"older's inequality to deduce that $\|\mathbf{x}\|^{d-1} \leqslant n^{\frac{d-2}{2}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Test the spectral norm on the conjugate of x^{[d-1]} and an eigenvector, then bound ||x||^{d-1} by Hoelder.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Eigenvector and dual vector
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathcal{T}\times (\otimes^{d-1}\mathbf{x})=\lambda \mathbf{x}^{(d-1)}$ and $|\lambda|=\rho(\mathcal{T})$. Normalize $\mathbf{x}$ by $\|\mathbf{x}^{(d-1)}\|=1$. Let $\mathbf{y}=\bar{\mathbf{x}}^{(d-1)}$, the complex conjugate of $\mathbf{x}^{(d-1)}$, so that $\|\mathbf{y}\|=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Take an eigenpair with |lambda| = rho, normalize, and set y = conj(x^{[d-1]}).
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Bound by the spectral norm
nodes.statement: Then $|\mathcal{T}\times(\mathbf{y}\otimes(\otimes^{d-1}\mathbf{x})|= |\lambda|$. Therefore $|\lambda|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\|\mathbf{y}\|\|\mathbf{x}\|^{d-1}=\|\mathcal{T}\|_\infty \|\mathbf{x}\|^{d-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Testing the spectral norm gives |lambda| <= ||T|| ||x||^{d-1}.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Hoelder bound
nodes.statement: Use H\"older's inequality to deduce that $\|\mathbf{x}\|^{d-1} \leqslant n^{\frac{d-2}{2}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Hoelder bounds ||x||^{d-1} by n^{(d-2)/2}.

nodes.name: Extension to non-partially-symmetric tensors
nodes.statement: In Lemma~\ref{specneqrad}, we assumed that $\mathcal{T}\in \mathbb{C}^{n^{\times d}}_{ps}$ since we only considered the eigenproblem for partially symmetric tensors. The inequality~\eqref{specneqrad1} carries over to any $\mathcal{T}\in \mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{C}^{n^{\times d}}$, understanding that $\rho(\mathcal{T})$ only depends of the partially symmetric part of $\mathcal{T}$.

nodes.name: Spectral norm of nonnegative tensors (8.3)
nodes.statement: \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}=\max\{\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j), \;\|\mathbf{x}_j\|=1, \mathbf{x}_j\geqslant \mathbf{0}, j\in[d]\} \textrm{ for } \mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathbf{m}}.

nodes.name: Inequalities for spectral norms of tensors
nodes.statement: $\;$ \begin{enumerate} \item For $\mathcal{T}=[t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}$ let $|\mathcal{T}|$ be the tensor in $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}$ whose entries are the absolute value of the entries $\mathcal{T}$: $|\mathcal{T}|=[|t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|]$. Then \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \||\mathcal{T}|\|_{\infty}. \end{equation} Furthermore \begin{equation} \max_{i_1\in[m_1],\cdots,i_d\in[m_d]}|t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}. \end{equation} \item Let $\mathbf{n}=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\in\mathbb{N}^k, \mathbf{m}=(m_1,\ldots,m_d)\in\mathbb{N}^d$. Assume that $\mathcal{E}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{n}}, \mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}$. Then \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{E}\otimes \mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}=\|\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty} \end{equation} \item Let us still make the assumptions of \emph{2}. Suppose furthermore that $\mathcal{E}$ is a subtensor of $\mathcal{T}$. Then \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\leqslant\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}. \end{equation} \item Assume that $\mathcal{E},\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}_+$. Then \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{E}\circ\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}. \end{equation} \item Let $D\subset \mathbb{R}^m$ be a convex set. Assume that $\mathcal{T}:D\to \mathbb{R}_+^{\mathbf{m}}$ is logconvex. Then $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}:D\to\mathbb{R}_+$ is logconvex. \item Let $\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\in\mathbb{R}_+^{\mathbf{m}}$. Then \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{F}^{\circ \alpha}\circ\mathcal{G}^{\circ\beta}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{F}\|_{\infty}^\alpha \|\mathcal{G}\|_{\infty}^\beta,\; \alpha,\beta> 0, \alpha+\beta=1. \end{equation} \item Assume that $\mathcal{T}=[t_{j_1,\ldots,j_d}]\in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}_+$. Then the function $\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|_{\infty}^{\frac{1}{s}}$ is a decreasing function on $(0,\infty)$. Furthermore \begin{equation} \lim_{s\to\infty} \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|_{\infty}^{\frac{1}{s}}=\max_{j_1\in[m_1],\ldots,j_d\in[m_k]} t_{j_1,\ldots,j_d}, \end{equation} is the standard $\ell_{\infty}$ norm of $\mathcal{T}$ viewed as a vector. \item Assume that $\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}_+$. Then \begin{eqnarray} &&\|\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty} \textrm{ if } \mathcal{E}\leqslant \mathcal{F},\\ &&\|\mathcal{T}\circ\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\|\mathcal{E}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \; \|\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathrm{pat}\; \mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\|\mathcal{E}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}. \end{eqnarray} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Eight properties of the spectral norm: domination by |T|, multiplicativity, subtensor monotonicity, Hadamard, log-convexity, Kingman and Karlin-Ost analogues, tropical bounds.

nodes.statement: &&\|\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty} \textrm{ if } \mathcal{E}\leqslant \mathcal{F},\\ &&\|\mathcal{T}\circ\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\|\mathcal{E}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \; \|\mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathrm{pat}\; \mathcal{E}\|_{\infty}\|\mathcal{E}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}.

nodes.label: increspropspectnrm

nodes.name: Proof of the spectral norm inequalities
nodes.statement: \emph{1}. As $|\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j)|\leqslant |\mathcal{T}|\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d|\mathbf{x}_j|)$, the maximal characterization of $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}$ and $\||\mathcal{T}|\|_{\infty}$ yields \eqref{absdomin}. By choosing $\mathbf{x}_j$ to be a canonical basis vector $(\delta_{1i_j},\ldots,\delta_{m_ji_j})^\top\in\mathbb{F}^{m_j}$ we deduce that $|\mathcal{T}\times (\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j))= |t_{i_1,\ldots,i_j}|$. Hence \eqref{lowbndspecnrm} holds. \emph{2}. The equality \eqref{specnrmtenprod} is a well known equality, which follows from \[(\mathcal{E}\otimes\mathcal{T})\times((\otimes_{i=1}^k \mathbf{x}_i)\otimes(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{y}_j))=(\mathcal{E}\times(\otimes_{i=1}^k \mathbf{x}_i))(\mathcal{T}\times (\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{y}_j)) \] and from the definition of the spectral norm. \emph{3}. The inequality\eqref{subtenin} follows straightforwardly from \eqref{defspecnrm} by considering $\mathbf{x}_j$ that have support on $I_j$. \emph{4}. The inequality \eqref{lowbndspecnrm} yields that \[\sum_{i_1\in[m_1],\ldots,i_d\in[m_d]} e_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|x_{j_1,1}|\cdots |x_{j_d,d}|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\!\!\!\! \sum_{i_1\in[m_1],\ldots,i_d\in[m_d]} e_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|x_{j_1,1}|\cdots |x_{j_d,d}|\] Apply now the characterization \eqref{infnrmnnc} to deduce the inequality \eqref{hadprodin}. \emph{5}. Clearly, if $\mathbf{x}_j\in\mathbb{R}^{m_j}_+$ for $j\in[d]$ then $\mathcal{T}(\mathbf{t})\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j)$ is a logconvex function for $\mathbf{t}\in D$. Recall that the maximum of logconvex functions is a logconvex function. The characterization \eqref{infnrmnnc} yields the logconvexity of $\|\mathcal{T}(\mathbf{t})\|_{\infty}$. \emph{6}. Assume that $\mathcal{F}=[f_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}],\mathcal{G}=[g_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]$, and $f_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}, g_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}>0$. Define a logconvex map $\mathcal{T}:\mathbb{R}^2\to \mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}_+$ by the equality $\mathcal{T}(s,t)=[f_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}^s g_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}^t]$. Clearly $(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha(1,0)+\beta(0,1)$. Hence the logconvexity of $\|\mathcal{T}(s,t)\|_{\infty}$ yields \eqref{genkinin1}. The general case in which some entries of $\mathcal{F}$ or $\mathcal{G}$ are zero follows from the continuity of the spectral norm. \emph{7}. For $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}$ denote by \[\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}=\max\{|t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|, i_j\in[m_j], j\in[d]\},\] the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm of $\mathcal{T}$ viewed as a vector. We shall use the inequalities: \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|\leqslant \sqrt{M(d)}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \quad M(d)=\prod_{j=1}^d m_j. \end{equation} Indeed, the first inequality is precisely~\eqref{lowbndspecnrm}. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality yield that $|\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d\mathbf{x}_j)|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\| \|\otimes_{j=1}^d\mathbf{x}_j\|$. Hence $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|$. The last inequality in~\eqref{uplowestspecnrm} is straightforward. Assume that $\mathcal{T}\geqslant 0$. Then \[\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|^{\frac{1}{s}}\leqslant M(d)^{\frac{1}{2s}}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \quad s>0.\] Let $s\to\infty$ to deduce \eqref{limspecnrm}. We now show that $\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|^{\frac{1}{s}}_{\infty}$ is a decreasing function for $s\in (0,\infty)$. It is enough to show that $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}^{\frac{1} {t}}$ for $t>1$. Fix $t>1$. Let $\mathbb{R}^2\to \mathbb{R}_+^{\mathbf{m}}$ be the logconvex map $(a,b)\mapsto \mathcal{T}(a,b)=\mathcal{T}^{\circ(a+b)}$. Hence $\log \|\mathcal{T}(a,b)\|_{\infty}$ is a convex function on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Assume that $s>t$. Note that \[(1,t-1)=\frac{t-1}{s-1}(1,s-1)+\frac{s-t}{s-1}(1,0).\] Hence \[\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \frac{(t-1)s}{(s-1)}\left(\frac{1}{s}\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|_\infty\right)+\frac{s-t}{(s-1)}\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}.\] Let $s\to\infty$ and use \eqref{limspecnrm} to deduce \begin{equation} \log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant (t-1)\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}+\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty} \end{equation} Use \eqref{uplowestspecnrm} to deduce $t\log \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \log \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}$. \emph{8}. The inequality \eqref{increspropspectnrm} follows straightforwardly from \eqref{infnrmnnc}. The first inequality of \eqref{ineqETtropnorm} follows from the inequality $\mathcal{T}\circ \mathcal{E}\leqslant \|\mathcal{E}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\mathcal{T}$ and \eqref{increspropspectnrm}. The second inequality of \eqref{ineqETtropnorm} follow from the first inequality of \eqref{ineqETtropnorm} by letting $\mathcal{T}=\mathrm{pat}\; \mathcal{E}$.
nodes.statement_short: Part-by-part: variational characterizations of the spectral norm, log-convexity of maxima of logconvex functions, and a convexity interpolation as s -> infinity.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Part 1
nodes.statement: \emph{1}. As $|\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j)|\leqslant |\mathcal{T}|\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d|\mathbf{x}_j|)$, the maximal characterization of $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}$ and $\||\mathcal{T}|\|_{\infty}$ yields \eqref{absdomin}. By choosing $\mathbf{x}_j$ to be a canonical basis vector $(\delta_{1i_j},\ldots,\delta_{m_ji_j})^\top\in\mathbb{F}^{m_j}$ we deduce that $|\mathcal{T}\times (\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j))= |t_{i_1,\ldots,i_j}|$. Hence \eqref{lowbndspecnrm} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Absolute values and coordinate vectors give (8.4)-(8.5).
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Part 2
nodes.statement: \emph{2}. The equality \eqref{specnrmtenprod} is a well known equality, which follows from \[(\mathcal{E}\otimes\mathcal{T})\times((\otimes_{i=1}^k \mathbf{x}_i)\otimes(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{y}_j))=(\mathcal{E}\times(\otimes_{i=1}^k \mathbf{x}_i))(\mathcal{T}\times (\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{y}_j)) \] and from the definition of the spectral norm.
nodes.statement_short: Product of separable test vectors gives multiplicativity.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Part 3
nodes.statement: \emph{3}. The inequality\eqref{subtenin} follows straightforwardly from \eqref{defspecnrm} by considering $\mathbf{x}_j$ that have support on $I_j$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict test vectors to the subtensor's supports.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Part 4
nodes.statement: \emph{4}. The inequality \eqref{lowbndspecnrm} yields that \[\sum_{i_1\in[m_1],\ldots,i_d\in[m_d]} e_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|x_{j_1,1}|\cdots |x_{j_d,d}|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\!\!\!\! \sum_{i_1\in[m_1],\ldots,i_d\in[m_d]} e_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|x_{j_1,1}|\cdots |x_{j_d,d}|\] Apply now the characterization \eqref{infnrmnnc} to deduce the inequality \eqref{hadprodin}.
nodes.statement_short: Entrywise bound and (8.3) give the Hadamard inequality.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Part 5
nodes.statement: \emph{5}. Clearly, if $\mathbf{x}_j\in\mathbb{R}^{m_j}_+$ for $j\in[d]$ then $\mathcal{T}(\mathbf{t})\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d \mathbf{x}_j)$ is a logconvex function for $\mathbf{t}\in D$. Recall that the maximum of logconvex functions is a logconvex function. The characterization \eqref{infnrmnnc} yields the logconvexity of $\|\mathcal{T}(\mathbf{t})\|_{\infty}$.
nodes.statement_short: A maximum of logconvex functions is logconvex.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Part 6
nodes.statement: \emph{6}. Assume that $\mathcal{F}=[f_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}],\mathcal{G}=[g_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}]$, and $f_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}, g_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}>0$. Define a logconvex map $\mathcal{T}:\mathbb{R}^2\to \mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}_+$ by the equality $\mathcal{T}(s,t)=[f_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}^s g_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}^t]$. Clearly $(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha(1,0)+\beta(0,1)$. Hence the logconvexity of $\|\mathcal{T}(s,t)\|_{\infty}$ yields \eqref{genkinin1}. The general case in which some entries of $\mathcal{F}$ or $\mathcal{G}$ are zero follows from the continuity of the spectral norm.
nodes.statement_short: Log-convexity along (s, t) gives the Kingman-type inequality.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Part 7
nodes.statement: \emph{7}. For $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}$ denote by \[\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}=\max\{|t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|, i_j\in[m_j], j\in[d]\},\] the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm of $\mathcal{T}$ viewed as a vector. We shall use the inequalities: \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|\leqslant \sqrt{M(d)}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \quad M(d)=\prod_{j=1}^d m_j. \end{equation} Indeed, the first inequality is precisely~\eqref{lowbndspecnrm}. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality yield that $|\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d\mathbf{x}_j)|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\| \|\otimes_{j=1}^d\mathbf{x}_j\|$. Hence $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|$. The last inequality in~\eqref{uplowestspecnrm} is straightforward. Assume that $\mathcal{T}\geqslant 0$. Then \[\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|^{\frac{1}{s}}\leqslant M(d)^{\frac{1}{2s}}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \quad s>0.\] Let $s\to\infty$ to deduce \eqref{limspecnrm}. We now show that $\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|^{\frac{1}{s}}_{\infty}$ is a decreasing function for $s\in (0,\infty)$. It is enough to show that $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}^{\frac{1} {t}}$ for $t>1$. Fix $t>1$. Let $\mathbb{R}^2\to \mathbb{R}_+^{\mathbf{m}}$ be the logconvex map $(a,b)\mapsto \mathcal{T}(a,b)=\mathcal{T}^{\circ(a+b)}$. Hence $\log \|\mathcal{T}(a,b)\|_{\infty}$ is a convex function on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Assume that $s>t$. Note that \[(1,t-1)=\frac{t-1}{s-1}(1,s-1)+\frac{s-t}{s-1}(1,0).\] Hence \[\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \frac{(t-1)s}{(s-1)}\left(\frac{1}{s}\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|_\infty\right)+\frac{s-t}{(s-1)}\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}.\] Let $s\to\infty$ and use \eqref{limspecnrm} to deduce \begin{equation} \log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant (t-1)\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}+\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty} \end{equation} Use \eqref{uplowestspecnrm} to deduce $t\log \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \log \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}$.
nodes.statement_short: Norm comparisons give the limit; interpolation shows monotonicity.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Norm comparisons
nodes.statement: \emph{7}. For $\mathcal{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbf{m}}$ denote by \[\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}=\max\{|t_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}|, i_j\in[m_j], j\in[d]\},\] the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm of $\mathcal{T}$ viewed as a vector. We shall use the inequalities: \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|\leqslant \sqrt{M(d)}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \quad M(d)=\prod_{j=1}^d m_j. \end{equation} Indeed, the first inequality is precisely~\eqref{lowbndspecnrm}. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality yield that $|\mathcal{T}\times(\otimes_{j=1}^d\mathbf{x}_j)|\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\| \|\otimes_{j=1}^d\mathbf{x}_j\|$. Hence $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|$. The last inequality in~\eqref{uplowestspecnrm} is straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Compare l_infty, spectral and Hilbert-Schmidt norms (8.13).
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Norm comparison (8.13)
nodes.statement: \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}\|\leqslant \sqrt{M(d)}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \quad M(d)=\prod_{j=1}^d m_j.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: uplowestspecnrm

nodes.name: Limit of Hadamard powers
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathcal{T}\geqslant 0$. Then \[\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\leqslant \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|^{\frac{1}{s}}\leqslant M(d)^{\frac{1}{2s}}\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}, \quad s>0.\] Let $s\to\infty$ to deduce \eqref{limspecnrm}.
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich and let s -> infinity for (8.10).
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Monotonicity in s
nodes.statement: We now show that $\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|^{\frac{1}{s}}_{\infty}$ is a decreasing function for $s\in (0,\infty)$. It is enough to show that $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}^{\frac{1} {t}}$ for $t>1$. Fix $t>1$. Let $\mathbb{R}^2\to \mathbb{R}_+^{\mathbf{m}}$ be the logconvex map $(a,b)\mapsto \mathcal{T}(a,b)=\mathcal{T}^{\circ(a+b)}$. Hence $\log \|\mathcal{T}(a,b)\|_{\infty}$ is a convex function on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Assume that $s>t$. Note that \[(1,t-1)=\frac{t-1}{s-1}(1,s-1)+\frac{s-t}{s-1}(1,0).\] Hence \[\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \frac{(t-1)s}{(s-1)}\left(\frac{1}{s}\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|_\infty\right)+\frac{s-t}{(s-1)}\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}.\] Let $s\to\infty$ and use \eqref{limspecnrm} to deduce \begin{equation} \log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant (t-1)\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}+\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty} \end{equation} Use \eqref{uplowestspecnrm} to deduce $t\log \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \log \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}$.
nodes.statement_short: ||T^{os}||^{1/s} is decreasing.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Reduce to t > 1
nodes.statement: It is enough to show that $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}^{\frac{1} {t}}$ for $t>1$. Fix $t>1$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to compare exponent t > 1 with 1.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Log-convex two-parameter family
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{R}^2\to \mathbb{R}_+^{\mathbf{m}}$ be the logconvex map $(a,b)\mapsto \mathcal{T}(a,b)=\mathcal{T}^{\circ(a+b)}$. Hence $\log \|\mathcal{T}(a,b)\|_{\infty}$ is a convex function on $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.statement_short: log ||T^{o(a+b)}|| is convex on R^2.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Convex interpolation
nodes.statement: Assume that $s>t$. Note that \[(1,t-1)=\frac{t-1}{s-1}(1,s-1)+\frac{s-t}{s-1}(1,0).\] Hence \[\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant \frac{(t-1)s}{(s-1)}\left(\frac{1}{s}\log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ s}\|_\infty\right)+\frac{s-t}{(s-1)}\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate between exponents 1 and s.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Let s -> infinity
nodes.statement: Let $s\to\infty$ and use \eqref{limspecnrm} to deduce \begin{equation} \log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant (t-1)\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}+\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty} \end{equation} Use \eqref{uplowestspecnrm} to deduce $t\log \|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}\geqslant \log \|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}$.
nodes.statement_short: Let s -> infinity and use (8.13).
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: Spectral norm power bound (8.14)
nodes.statement: \log\|\mathcal{T}^{\circ t}\|_{\infty}\leqslant (t-1)\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}+\log\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors
nodes.label: specnrmtin

nodes.name: Part 8
nodes.statement: \emph{8}. The inequality \eqref{increspropspectnrm} follows straightforwardly from \eqref{infnrmnnc}. The first inequality of \eqref{ineqETtropnorm} follows from the inequality $\mathcal{T}\circ \mathcal{E}\leqslant \|\mathcal{E}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}\mathcal{T}$ and \eqref{increspropspectnrm}. The second inequality of \eqref{ineqETtropnorm} follow from the first inequality of \eqref{ineqETtropnorm} by letting $\mathcal{T}=\mathrm{pat}\; \mathcal{E}$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity from (8.3) and T o E <= ||E||_infty T; then T = pat E.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors

nodes.name: l_infty norm as tropical spectral norm
nodes.statement: In view of \eqref{limspecnrm} $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell_{\infty}}$ can be considered as a tropical version of $\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\infty}$ for a nonnegative tensor. Hence the inequalities \eqref{ineqETtropnorm} are analogs of the inequalities \eqref{rhotropin1} -- \eqref{rhotropin2}.
nodes.section: 8 Inequalities for spectral norms of nonnegative tensors
